Blanket write-denial for the session agent contradicts our Working Mode, which routes small tasks inline. On its own terms it is leaky: the git allowlist has no default-deny arm — push --force, reset --hard, clean -fd all fall through to exit 0 (:126-147, :167), all of which our block-dangerous-commands.sh denies — and the --no-verify test matches any '-n' substring (:138), denying innocent commits. The one good fragment, a bd create description floor (:154-161), is deferred: it would misfire on our thin idea-bead flow without an -l idea exemption, and we lack evidence thin beads cause rework.

The gap it closes is real — nothing stops dispatching an implementer with no tracked bead — but the mechanical check needs a convention we have not mandated: a bead id field in every dispatch brief. Re-open when the execution skill's brief format requires that field; then this becomes a one-check PreToolUse:Task hook.

Three checks: the closed-bead guard (:29-35) is a genuine gap for us (closed beads are our durable rejection record with nothing preventing a re-claim) and is deferred into bead cr-ghw; the blocker check is redundant for us (bd ready --parent is dependency-truth by construction); the design-doc check presupposes the architect flow that deadlocks at this pin. Only the first survives, as cr-ghw.

reasoning: Enforces edits-only-in-worktrees; presupposes worktree-per-task, which we do not run — our review packages the working tree because implementers do not commit.

Same worktree/branch model presupposition, and internally contradictory at the pin: it forces children onto a shared bd-{EPIC_ID} branch while the worker template creates bd-{BEAD_ID} per child and validate-completion.sh checks the remote for the per-child branch that the shared model never creates. Also half-broken: primary detection reads a .conversation_context field the event does not supply.

TCP's flagship gate, and the strongest single reason to distrust the framework's enforcement claims: it reads .agent_transcript_path — not a documented SubagentStop field — and explicitly approves-and-exits when it is empty (:7, :11), so it fails open; its block shape ({"decision":"block"}) is also undocumented for SubagentStop. Even granting the plumbing, it checks only bookkeeping (worktree exists, tree clean, branch pushed, status inreview, response length) and never test evidence — 'Tests: pass' is a literal template string the worker fills in. Our verification-before-completion is a strictly better specification; the mechanizable subset (epic-close) goes to cr-ghw instead.

The shipped implementation is a no-op: it reads a CLAUDE_TOOL_INPUT env var Claude Code never sets and exits 0 (:8, :11), and its own test drives it the same wrong way (tests/test-validate-epic-close.sh:37) — a suite validating the mock. But CHECK 2 (deny closing an epic with open children) is exactly the jq check our execution skill states as prose (execution/SKILL.md:89-93); deferred into bead cr-ghw as a stdin-driven reimplementation with a named override. CHECK 1 (merged-PR required) is rejected — it would deadlock our conservative commit/push authority.
debts: stdin-driven reimplementation of the children-closed check lives in bead cr-ghw
